text: A plan's check runs only its acceptance tests (#487). Before a built-in Go plan is proposed, the planner's check tool and the factory's own check compile the packages that hold its acceptance tests and run each of those tests once. gofmt, go vet and the tests of every package the plan touches run in a build's checks alone. What a plan's check decides never read them: it refuses an acceptance test that already passes, a deadline, an interruption or unfinished acceptance evidence, so those phases could refuse a draft only through their own time-outs, as they did #669's on 11-06 and #947's on 11-19. #947's check ran the 775 tests of the three packages it touched before its seven acceptance tests, and ran out of its twelve minutes beside three other sandboxes on the same machine, after the agent's own check of the same plan had passed in 6 minutes 16 seconds. On main, with a cold cache and no other sandbox, the check of a plan shaped like #947's took 3 minutes 16 seconds before the change and 37 seconds after. A configured repository's base check still runs each touched part's commands before its selectors.
